items.stem: In a tool-use interaction, which component actually runs the tool and returns a result to the model?

options.text: The application code, which executes the tool and sends the result back
options.rationale: Correct: the model requests a tool call; the application runs it and returns the result.

options.text: The model runs the tool internally
options.rationale: The model only emits a tool-use request; it does not execute the tool.

options.text: The end user runs the tool manually each time
The tool runs itself with no caller
options.rationale: A caller must invoke the tool.

items.explanation: Correct: the model requests a tool call; the application runs it and returns the result.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make structured output safer to rely on? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validate the output against the expected schema before using it
options.rationale: Correct: validation catches malformed or missing fields.

options.text: Retry or repair when validation fails
options.rationale: Correct: a failed validation should trigger a controlled retry, not silent use.

options.text: Assume any returned JSON is correct
options.rationale: Returned structure can still be wrong; it must be checked.

options.text: Remove all field constraints to avoid errors
options.rationale: Dropping constraints makes bad output more likely, not safer.

items.explanation: Correct: validation catches malformed or missing fields.

items.stem: A write tool may be called twice for the same request after a retry. What design prevents duplicate side-effects?

options.text: Make the tool idempotent so repeating the call has no additional effect
options.rationale: Correct: idempotent design makes retries safe.
Blocking retries harms reliability and does not address duplicates generally.

options.text: Ignore the second call silently with no safeguard
options.rationale: Silently ignoring is not a controlled safeguard.

options.text: Let the model decide whether to repeat the action
options.rationale: Safety should be enforced in the contract, not left to the model.

items.explanation: Correct: idempotent design makes retries safe.
